outcome: Admission to the intensive care unit
cohort: The study included 8,340 singletons ≥ 14 weeks with recorded BMI who delivered at a Level IV center over two consecutive years.
finding: Parturients with BMI ≥ 30 had a higher risk of hemorrhage-related morbidity compared with patients with BMI < 30, primarily due to increased risk of blood loss ≥ 1,000 mL and uterotonic use.
mod_finding: Increased risk for CMHO was only present in BMI ≥ 40 for vaginal deliveries and only for BMI of 30 to 39.9 in cesarean deliveries.
